sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Internet Retailing of Outdoor Sports and Camping Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (Metropolitan and overseas departments as integrated parts of the unitary Republic)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic legal family), with Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Civil Code (Code civil) and Administrative Law; EU supranational law prevails
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Income Tax Convention of Aug 31, 1994, as amended by the Jan 13, 2009 Protocol
France–China (PRC) Income Tax Convention signed Nov 29, 1984, as amended by the Protocol of Dec 1, 2013
France–China (PRC) Bilateral Investment Protection Agreement (EU-China bilateral investment protection framework under negotiation; existing national BIT of May 30, 1984 remains applicable partially)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention of July 19, 2008, and the EU–UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA)
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (BEPS MLI), ratified by France on Nov 24, 2021

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title VII, Chapter VII — Articles L.227-1 through L.227-32 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Article L.210-6 (legal personality upon registration); Articles R.210-1 to R.210-8 and R.123-1 et seq. (RCS filing formalities); Décret n°67-236 and related regulatory acts as codified.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; filings are made through the INPI 'Guichet unique électronique'.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise / formulaire M0 (Cerfa n°13627*06) — transmitted as part of the electronic 'Dossier unique d'immatriculation au RCS' through the INPI portail.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legally prescribed minimum share capital; a zero-EUR capital is permitted. Where a positive capital is adopted, cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations account and may be withdrawn only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a report by a statutory appraiser (commissaire aux apports) unless an exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The shareholders have approved and adopted the articles of association and have subscribed the full share capital; any cash contributions are deposited as required by law in a blocked account pending RCS registration. RESOLVED: The registered office of the SAS is fixed at [address], within the jurisdiction of the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce of [city]. RESOLVED: [Name] is appointed President with authority to sign, open bank accounts and complete all registration, licensing and post-formation formalities. RESOLVED: All actions conducted in connection with incorporation are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the articles of association ('statuts') and issue of share subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: No government filing at this stage; preparer may be an avocat or notaire; notarial deed optional unless the founders request it.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS articles in French, setting out corporate name, domicile, purpose, duration, capital, classes of shares, voting and leadership rules, powers of the President, and dispute-resolution provisions. Have each shareholder sign the articles and a written share-subscription list. If in-kind contributions are made, arrange a report by a statutory appraiser (commissaire aux apports) unless an exemption applies.
required_dossiers: Completed draft statutes in French
Share subscription and contribution reports
Identity documents of establishing shareholders and President
Proof of legal capacity and powers of attorneys for corporate shareholders ('attestation de pouvoir')
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: This is a pre-registration step; if the greffe later rejects the statutes for ambiguity, amend the statutes by unanimous shareholder decision and resubmit; no formal appeal is required at that point.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of cash capital in a blocked account and receipt of a certificate of consignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French bank, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or notary in charge of the consignment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a positive share capital is adopted, cause each cash contribution to be paid into a special account opened in the name of the company in formation. The depositary issues a 'certificat du dépositaire des fonds' ('attestation de dépôt des fonds') stating the balance, which is required for the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Identity documents of the subscriber and President
Power to open bank account if signed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses because of KYC issues, provide corporate ultimate-beneficial-owner evidence and a French passport/residence permit; choose an alternative bank or notary. The funds are retained until registration certificate is produced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the constitution notice in a Journal d'annonces légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An approved legal-notice newspaper (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office; list maintained by the French State and issued by the Préfecture.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the mandatory legal announcement indicating corporate form, name, capital, registered office, object, duration, President details and the RCS registration court. Obtain the publisher's official attestation of insertion ('exemplaire justificatif de publication') to attach to the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: SAS statutes (draft or signed)
Certified copy of the share-subscription and capital-deposit evidence
Name, address and details of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette for the wrong territorial department is used, publish again in the correct JAL; there is no extra registry fee but the announcement fee must be re-paid. The registry will reject available prior if department mismatch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the registration file through the INPI Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique électronique / Portail des formalités des entreprises at www.guichet-entreprises.fr operated by INPI; transmits to the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the legal document online, upload the signed statutes, legal-announcement certificate, certificate of authority, and capital-deposit certificate (or statement in the articles if capital is €0). Pay the registry fee through the portal. The INPI dispatches to the competent registry and generates a formal receipt.
required_dossiers: M0/déclaration d'immatriculation (electronic)
Signed statutes in French
Attestation de publication dans un JAL
Certificat du dépositaire des fonds (if capital paid)
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE)
Justificatif of registered office (domiciliation lease, free-occupation certificate or home-sharing declaration)
Current identity document of the President and any authorised signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is refused for formal defects, the applicant receives a 'rejet/interruption' notice with an online correction deadline; correct the dossier in the 'suivi de formalités' account. For alleged material irregularities, submit a formal complaint/recours to the INPI, then to the Juge du registre.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration on the RCS and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce / CCI business formalities centre under the control of the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of legal controls, the registry registers the company in the RCS, assigns the SIREN/SIRET numbers, and publishes an 'insertion au Bodacc' where required. The company acquires legal personality only at this date and time. Download the certified 'extrait Kbis' from the repository, which acts as the company's identity certificate.
required_dossiers: Transmitted dossier from step 4
Receipt of registry fees
Copy of the filed statutes annotated as 'certifié conforme' by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry delays beyond the legal deadlines, contact the greffe and, if necessary, apply to the Juge chargé du contrôle des registres to order registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration administrative and tax formalities (employer registration and corporate governance filings)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, DGFiP, INSEE and the company's services (electronic portals: 'Déclarations sociales', 'Gérer mon entreprise' at impots.gouv.fr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the numéro SIREN, open the company's bank accounts in the company name, register as an employer with URSSAF if hiring begins, declare the company within 15 days to the competent tax office if not automatically done, file the beneficial-ownership declaration with the registry, and adopt a first President's resolution addressing bank account mandates, professional insurance, VAT treatment, and commencement of activity. Update the RCS if the business activity changes.
required_dossiers: Kbis and SIREN/SIRET
Decisions of shareholder/president or 'PV de décision'
Bank account opening forms
Declaration of commencement of activity for the tax office if not automatic
Office/warehouse lease and occupational certification if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGFiP notifies missing data, respond within 30 days via the professional online tax area. Late registrations may incur penalties, but a corrective declaration can be filed with URSSAF/DGFiP and payment/reduction requested when due to circumstances beyond control.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to pure e-commerce retail. The DREAL / local Préfecture is the competent authority only where a storage warehouse qualifies as an installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) under rubrique 1510.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None. A SAS engaged solely in internet retailing does not require an exploitation permit. Physical or warehouse activity, if later established, may require a declaration/enregistrement as an ICPE.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires / Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR); locally enforced by the DREAL / Direction de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment for the declared e-commerce retail activity and offices. A covered warehouse used for storage may be subject to the ICPE declaration/registration regime under rubrique 1510 of the nomenclature des installations classées if its size is above the regulatory thresholds, in which case the DREAL determines whether an evaluation (étude d'impact) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission points from retail operations. Sanitary wastewater must meet municipal pre-treatment conditions where sewer discharge occurs. Waste handling must comply with Code de l'environnement waste hierarchy and sorting duties; packaging and electrical/electronic equipment obligations apply under the REP schemes, including eco-organismes such as Citeo and ecosystem/ecologic for batteries and EEE sold with camping gear.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Commercial premises must comply with Code du travail fire-safety rules (access, extinguishers, means of egress, periodic fire checks) and electrical installation safety verifications by a competent service. If a physical retail/showroom is open to the public, it may be classified as ERP and require fire-safety approval from the commission de sécurité. For warehouses/offices not open to the public, fire-safety compliance is evidenced by internal checks and insurance inspections. Structural load of existing buildings is attested by the landlord's or structural engineer's certificate, and workplaces must maintain a risk assessment (DUERP) and meet occupational health clearance requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE); foreign businesses are generally administered by the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). Official portal: impots.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the French business formalities one-stop shop (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises), operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The registration process results in allocation of a SIREN and SIRET number and tax registration with the DGFiP. The French VAT identification number is generally in the format FR followed by a two-digit control key and the entity's SIREN. A non-established foreign entity making taxable supplies in France must apply for French VAT registration with the DGFiP, generally through the SIEE or the competent tax service. It must provide incorporation documents, proof of business activity, identification of directors and beneficial owners, evidence of taxable transactions, bank and contact details, and, where applicable, a French fiscal representative. Entities established outside the European Union generally require a French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual assistance arrangement or specific exemption applies. OSS registration may be used for qualifying intra-EU distance sales and certain electronic commerce supplies, but it does not replace a French VAT registration where domestic taxable transactions or other registration obligations arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). An eligible SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu) under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, subject to statutory ownership, age, activity, size and duration conditions; the election is generally limited to five financial years and is not a general check-the-box election. A SASU may also have access to specific income-tax options subject to statutory conditions. France has no United States-style entity classification election. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive and do not constitute an elective pass-through classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), supplemented for qualifying cross-border electronic commerce by the Union One Stop Shop (OSS) and Import One Stop Shop (IOSS) regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general French VAT registration threshold applies to a non-established business carrying out taxable transactions in France. For French-established businesses eligible for the franchise en base de TVA, the principal annual turnover threshold for sales of goods and equivalent retail activities is EUR 85,000, with a higher tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500, subject to the applicable tax year and statutory rules. For qualifying intra-EU distance sales and certain electronically supplied services, the Union-wide EUR 10,000 annual threshold applies; above that threshold, VAT is generally due in the customer's Member State, with OSS available as a compliance mechanism. The French franchise thresholds do not eliminate VAT registration where the business voluntarily opts into VAT, makes intra-EU acquisitions, imports goods, or performs transactions for which registration is otherwise required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory electronic invoicing and transaction reporting on a staged basis. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations apply from that date to large and intermediate-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 to small and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory implementation rules. Domestic B2B electronic invoices will generally be transmitted through an approved private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, PDP), with the public portal serving the state reporting infrastructure. The system is based on structured invoice exchange and transmission of transaction and payment data, rather than universal real-time invoice clearance at the time of issuance. Cross-border B2B transactions and B2C transactions may require e-reporting rather than domestic B2B e-invoice transmission. Current VAT invoices and records must remain compliant with French authenticity, integrity, legibility, retention and audit-trail requirements. Retail B2C sales generally do not require an invoice unless requested or otherwise required, but VAT receipts and cash-register controls may apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT if the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by the seller or by a qualifying customer and the exporter can substantiate the physical exit from the EU. The exemption normally requires a valid customs export procedure, consistency between commercial, transport and customs records, and retention of proof of exit. Intra-EU supplies of goods are generally exempt as intra-Community supplies rather than exports, subject to customer VAT identification, transport evidence, recapitulative statement and other conditions. Services are not automatically zero-rated: the place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies. Certain services supplied to non-established business customers may be outside the scope of French VAT, while services directly connected with exported goods or qualifying international transport may benefit from specific exemptions. Export VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices, deductible business use, compliance with filing requirements and evidence that the underlying transactions satisfy the applicable exemption or place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration containing the correct exporter, consignee, commodity classification, customs procedure and statistical data
MRN and electronic proof of exit from the European Union, including the customs exit result or equivalent certified exit evidence
Commercial invoice, packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note or courier manifest
Purchase orders, sales contracts, delivery records and accounting entries linking the goods to the export transaction
Evidence of export-related freight, insurance and logistics arrangements where relevant
Customer and destination records sufficient to demonstrate dispatch to a non-EU destination

Inward remittance evidence only where required by a financing, banking, contractual or audit policy; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a statutory condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration may deny or claw back export VAT exemption where export evidence is missing, contradictory, late, falsified or insufficient to prove exit from the EU. The resulting VAT, interest for late payment and applicable penalties may be assessed retrospectively, generally within the statutory limitation period, subject to fraud and other extended-period rules. Deliberate or serious inaccuracies may trigger tax penalties based on the nature and gravity of the conduct, including penalties for bad faith or fraudulent manoeuvres; fraudulent conduct may also create criminal exposure. Customs infringements can result in additional customs debt, administrative penalties, seizure or forfeiture measures. Input VAT refunds may be reduced or refused where invoices, business purpose, payment records, transport evidence or export substantiation are deficient. France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days for ordinary export proceeds; any 180-day requirement would arise only from a specific financing, banking, grant or contractual arrangement rather than the general French VAT regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), exercising delegated foreign-exchange, balance-of-payments and financial-stability functions under the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF), within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) of the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully and freely convertible in both the current and capital accounts. France applies complete current-account liberalisation under Articles 63-66 TFEU and the EU Code of Liberalisation; capital movements within the EU/EEA are unrestricted, and movements vis-à-vis third countries are covered by the EU grandfathering regime (Regulation (EC) No 1869/2005). No exchange-control licence, prior central-bank authorisation or documentary approval is required to open foreign-currency accounts, to hold USD/CNY/GBP receipts, or to remit distributable profits to foreign shareholders. The only operative control is indirect: the SAS's banks file balance-of-payments declarations (opérations de change) with the Banque de France for each transaction at or above EUR 12,500. Profit remittance from an SAS is unrestricted, but is subject to a shareholder dividend resolution, standard AML documentation, and French withholding tax (25% for distributions decided in 2024, 26.5% in 2025, 25% from 2026) unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying EU corporate shareholder or under an applicable double-tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio apply to export proceeds in France. A French SAS may retain export receipts indefinitely in authorised foreign-currency settlement accounts (comptes en devises) and may convert them at its commercial discretion and at market-competitive pricing. The sole compliance duties are: (i) the customs export declaration (SAD/DAU) at the point of shipment; and (ii) the periodic balance-of-payments statistical declaration filed by the instructing credit institution to the Banque de France, using the OECD purpose code S2000 (trade in goods) and the transaction reference. No percentage of export receipts must be converted into EUR and no conversion timeline is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte courant) plus dedicated Capital Escrow Account (compte de dépôt de fonds) during incorporation, with multi-currency sub-accounts for USD and CNY
Operational Account with foreign-currency current accounts (comptes en devises) and trade-finance lines for L/C issuance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. network (Caisses Régionales / LCL)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and SEPA-clearing treasury account with cash-pooling capability
Operational Account with documentary-collection and L/C advisory/confirmation lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for French-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions operating under PSD2: Qonto S.A. (ACPR-licensed, PSAN-registered) and Shine (Société Générale group) provide fully remote onboarding, French IBANs and SEPA Instant clearing suitable for Stripe and PayPal collections. Offshore EU EMIs and neobanks (Wise Europe and Revolut Bank UAB, passporting into France under PSD2/branch registration) are viable as secondary collection or disbursement accounts but are rated Medium as sole treasury counterparties because safeguarding arrangements, contingency funds and trade-finance capabilities do not fully support L/Cs, FX forwards or high-limit documentary disbursements. Legal constraint: the SAS must verify ACPR/EBA register listing, segregated safeguarding of client funds under Articles L526-1 et seq. CMF, and the EMI's French reimbursement plan (fonds de garantie) before concentrating treasury balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not mandatory for a low-risk SAS under French law. Articles L561-5 et seq. CMF and ACPR 2021 AML guidelines permit fully remote corporate onboarding via verified digital identification (double-sided ID with liveness video) and e-signature (signature électronique); tier-1 banks routinely open accounts remotely for French-registered entities with a valid siège social and attested director address. However, the bank's commercial committee may require one physical or video meeting when the UBO is a non-EU/EEA resident, or when high foreign-currency clearing limits, trade-finance issuance or derivatives lines above EUR 100,000 are requested. Directors absent from France may sign under a notarised or apostilled power of attorney (procuration). The final mandate remains at the bank's risk-appetite discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or delayed Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing at the RCS - the mandatory French UBO registry that banks verify first and a dominant cause of account refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extrait Kbis (RCS extract) evidencing the RBE registration, the e-filed statuts (articles of association), an UBO organigramme identifying every natural person holding at least 25% of shares or voting rights, and passport/ID copies of each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce payment aggregation (Stripe/PayPal flows) flagged for anonymous third-party collections, chargeback volatility, or a mismatch between declared activity and processed volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Stripe and PayPal service agreements, monthly settlement statements (relevés de flux) with transaction detail, a 3-month ERP order/fulfilment export, the SAS's published terms and conditions (CGV) and privacy policy, and a chargeback-dispute register demonstrating disciplined resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid projected turnover or high transaction velocity inconsistent with a newly incorporated SAS, matching money-laundering typologies for fictitious e-commerce merchants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan with pro-forma revenue waterfall, VAT registration certificate (extrait RCS with n° intracommunautaire FR), supplier contracts and purchase orders for initial inventory, 3PL logistics agreements, and the live refund/return policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or non-EEA source of subscription capital triggering 'source of wealth' and 'source of funds' inquiries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference from the shareholder's home institution, tax assessments (avis d'imposition) or wealth declarations, sale or gift deeds (acte de cession / acte de donation) where applicable, and the SWIFT trail proving the funds were wired from the shareholder's regulated account to the French escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Domiciliation at a shared or virtual business-address provider (domiciliation commerciale) perceived as shell-company indicia.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated domiciliation contract with a legally registered gestionnaire de domiciliation (Article L123-11-2 Code de commerce), the SAS's commercial lease or co-working membership agreement, and a current utility bill in the SAS's legal name.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital contributions and shareholder loans (comptes courants d'associés) must arrive via SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 pacs.008) from the investor's regulated bank. Required data: OECD purpose code S1800 (direct investment - equity capital) or S1810 (shareholder loan), EUR or named foreign currency, and remittance narrative 'Apport en capital - [SAS legal name] - [deed/reference]'. The receiving bank files the Banque de France foreign-direct-investment (IDE) statistical declaration; because e-commerce retail of camping equipment is not in the Art. L151-3 CMF sensitive-sector list, a non-EU/EEA investor needs no prior authorisation, only the post-hoc IDE/balance-of-payments declaration. Supporting documents: shareholder resolution (procès-verbal d'assemblée générale), capital-subscription deed (acte de souscription) for contributions in kind, the bank's capital-deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds), and, for injections above EUR 1 million, the corporate-group structure chart and ultimate-investor identity file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements will clear through four rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer via the French STET/ECB-TIPS platforms for EUR supplier payments across the EU, with same-day or T+1 execution and low per-transaction cost; (ii) SWIFT MT103 / ISO 20022 pacs.008 single-customer credit transfers for USD, CNY and GBP invoice payments, carrying the correct OECD purpose code (S2100 for goods-related payments such as freight, or the specific merchandise code) and full structured remittance data; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) governed by UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for high-value bulk imports of camping hardware and textiles from Asia, issued by the French anchor bank and advised through the beneficiary's confirming bank; and (iv) documentary collections (Cash against Documents, D/P) for mid-size supplier balances. All outbound wires are screened against EU restrictive measures, UN sanctions and OFAC lists; the bank requires the pro-forma invoice, purchase contract and HS tariff classification code for every transfer above EUR 5,000, with the SAS retaining the full evidential trail (commande, facture, certificat de conformité CE/UKCA) per disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot and outright forward contracts (achat/vente à terme de devises) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF and EUR/JPY, documented under the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement and permitted under Articles L211-1 et seq. CMF when consistent with forecast commercial exposure; no underlying-lot certificate is demanded for amounts within the bank's market-risk envelope.

FX swaps (swaps de change) and cross-currency swaps for treasury rebalancing of foreign-currency settlement accounts and for hedging a foreign-currency shareholder loan or the EUR revolving credit facility, executed under the ISDA 2002/FBF framework with the anchor bank's market-risk desk.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - admissible only for thin-market or restricted-convertibility currencies where no onshore deliverable forward is available to a French corporate counterparty; expressly not permitted for EUR/USD or other G10 pairs with a liquid deliverable market, as such use would constitute speculative trading outside the SAS's corporate-object capacity (ultra vires) and would be rejected by compliance.

Vanilla FX options (achat d'options de change - calls and puts) for asymmetric protection of import margins on seasonal promotional inventory purchases; premiums are paid in full up-front, no naked short-option positions are permitted for a non-financial SAS, and execution is limited to regulated European counterparties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS via Guichet Unique (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end (e.g., by June 30 for December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice after one month; public notice of non-compliance; referral to the Public Prosecutor; risk of administrative strike-off from the RCS; fixed fine of EUR 46 per missing document.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration (liassez fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities by May 3 (normal actual regime) or May 16 (simplified regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of the tax due plus monthly interest of 0.20% (10% additional after 30 days); possible tax assessment upon non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly CA3 due by the 19th of the following month; annual CA12 under simplified regime due by the second business day after May 1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the VAT due plus monthly interest; possible reassessment and temporary withdrawal of VAT deduction rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Exceeding two of three thresholds at fiscal year-end triggers mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average headcount > 50.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation; the RCS beneficial-owner register is event-driven and must be updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers. Annual accounts filing includes representation that current UBO information remains accurate.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for sub-threshold SAS; if triggered, market range USD 6,000–15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs; R&D tax credit (up to 5% of eligible R&D expenses); patent box regime (10% rate on qualifying IP income)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat (DR) - Corporate tax return form, filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for calendar-year companies)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of taxable result before tax adjustments and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must file through a French tax representative or declare via permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for operating expenses, depreciation, and specific provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses attributable to French-source activities are deductible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of tax credits including R&D credit and other incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Eligibility restricted to French operations or qualifying cross-border transactions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 0.75% of tax due per month of delay (maximum 5% of tax due); late payment interest at 0.2% per month; criminal sanctions for willful non-compliance

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% flat rate for non-resident shareholders (reduced rates apply under applicable double tax treaties, e.g., 5% for substantial holdings)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from home jurisdiction and submit relevant forms (e.g., 2874) via impots.gouv.fr to claim reduced withholding tax rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 5% or 10% based on treaty (0% under many EU treaties); Interest: 0% under most treaties or 10-15% otherwise

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated group revenue for local file requirement
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities engaged in relevant activities; retail trading operations generally do not trigger full ESR but intra-group transactions require commercial rationale and economic substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable income or overstating deductible expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 500% of the evaded tax amount
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for tax restitution, penalties, and potential criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a company without economic substance or real business operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 500% of turnover, potential dissolution of the company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and possible imprisonment for fraudulent incorporation or management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or maintain transfer pricing documentation or using non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from €10,000 to €100,000 per violation plus tax adjustments and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face personal liability for restitution of additional taxes and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring transactions to evade anti-money laundering reporting or KYC requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million and imprisonment up to 1 year
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability and disqualification from management roles
